findings.summary: The driver change at the root cause has no demonstration of its own; criterion 1's end-to-end test skips it.
findings.evidence: In the lifecycle test the fake producer returns InvocationOutcome::TimedOut directly, so claude.rs is never run. If claude.rs still mapped a deadline to Killed (claude.rs:413), the lifecycle test would still pass, while real deadline kills would keep closing as failed. The 'fails without' claim ('with the driver … unchanged') is therefore not accurate for the driver half. The existing claude.rs test `a_timed_out_invocation_is_killed_with_a_lower_bound` (line 667) runs the real deadline path, and Step 2 already says it will be adjusted. Fix: Add that claude.rs test, renamed and asserting InvocationOutcome::TimedOut with detail 'deadline of Ns reached', to the criterion 1 demonstration (`cargo test -p athena-agent claude`). Also add the kill-switch test asserting Killed, so the case that must not be resumable is shown too.

findings.summary: Existing lifecycle tests use Killed with a deadline detail; their meaning changes and they need a decision.
findings.evidence: lifecycle.rs:1176-1178 scripts outcome Killed with detail 'deadline of 1800s reached' and asserts OutcomeState::Failed at line 1189. Once Killed means only the kill switch, this fixture describes a state the driver can no longer produce. Fix: Change the detail in these fixtures to a kill-switch text, or switch them to TimedOut and update the expected state. Also check that the cost-bound checks (lower-bound tokens, cap-bounded cost, check_history clean) still hold for a TimedOut invocation.

findings.summary: Changing the driver also changes verifier, critic and other role records to timed_out. Docs should say so, and every role's handling should be checked.
findings.evidence: The claude driver serves every role, so a verifier deadline will now record invocation outcome timed_out. The callers I read compare against `!= Success`, so behavior stays failed. That is consistent with the out-of-scope note, but the record does change for those roles. Fix: In docs/records.md and the CHANGELOG, say the timed_out invocation outcome applies to any role, and that only the producer stage keeps work. Grep for `== InvocationOutcome::Killed` and for matches over InvocationOutcome, beyond the compiler-reported ones, to confirm nothing keys on Killed for bounds.
findings.location: Files: claude.rs, docs/records.md; run.rs:708,1878; auditor.rs:333; steward.rs:943; reading.rs:341

findings.summary: Skipping admission for the kept candidate records partial work as an unchecked candidate.
findings.evidence: On the success path, admission (personal data, file size, capability rules) runs on the candidate commit before it is kept (run.rs:1598-1638). The plan writes a candidate record with empty violations and no admission run. A reader of the records cannot tell this from an admitted candidate, and the retry seeds from it. Fix: Run admission on the timed-out candidate and record any violations without failing the job. Or mark the candidate record clearly as unadmitted partial work. Either way the retry's own candidate still goes through admission.

findings.summary: The progress note's 'commands run' and changed paths need redacting like the other retry seed texts.
findings.evidence: tree_retry_seed redacts its texts with redactor.redact_all before putting them in the brief. The progress note puts commands run (which can hold arguments) into both records and the brief. Fix: Pass the note text through the redactor before writing progress-note.md and before embedding it in the brief.

summary: I read claude.rs, run.rs, reading.rs, lifecycle.rs and retry.rs. The code matches what the plan says. claude.rs:367/413 folds a deadline into Killed. The producer loop at run.rs:1440 closes the job failed on any non-Success outcome, before the candidate commit is built at run.rs:1583-1595. earlier_attempt_with (reading.rs:887) and qualifies_for_tree_retry/tree_retry_seed (reading.rs:1058-1156) accept only Rejected/Failed jobs with a verification record. run.rs:206 tree_seed and retry.rs:470 run_retry exist. So the plan fixes the fault where it starts: the driver stops misclassifying the deadline, and the producer loop stops dropping the edits. It reuses the existing tree-seed retry path, keeps the change additive in serde, and stays in the producer-only scope. The demonstrations exercise keep, resume, status and legacy deserialization with the fake agent, and each would fail without the change. Remaining issues are minor: (1) the driver half of the root cause is shown only by a claude.rs unit test that the demonstrations do not name; (2) existing Killed-with-deadline fixtures need a decision; (3) docs should say that the timed_out invocation outcome now appears for every role; (4) the kept candidate skips admission without saying so in its record; (5) the progress note should be redacted. Athena's findings on files outside the listed deliverables are justified: the listed deliverables were guesses, and these files are where the behavior lives. Accept.
